note.question: How does economic distress change brand switching between national and private labels, retailer/manufacturer pricing, and welfare across income groups, and what do subsidy or price-control policies do?
note.overview: The analytical model is an explicit Stackelberg channel game: the national-brand manufacturer sets wholesale price, the retailer sets national/private-label prices under shelf capacity, and heterogeneous consumers choose brands.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

models.method: The paper estimates that, on average, there was an additional increase of 1.6% in expenditures on private-label products by high-income consumers (beyond what low-income consumers experienced) during the economic recession of 2007–2009 using NielsenIQ’s Homescan Panel data and a difference-in-differences approach.

sources.quote: High-income consumers perceive significantly more risk in purchasing private-label products than low-income consumers, possibly because of differing expectations and experiences with product quality (Beneke 2013).

components.label: Subgame-perfect Stackelberg channel-pricing equilibrium
